message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I'm player p2 in a 1v1 against p1. I just passed GO and landed on Community Chest. I have $1861 cash and three hotels on St. Charles Place, States Avenue, and Virginia Avenue. I'm not in jail.

I rolled a 10 from North Carolina to pass GO and land on Community Chest. My cash is $1861, which differs from the expected $1911 after receiving $200.

The $50 gap in cash likely came from a Community Chest payment. I hold two get-out-of-jail cards. My opponent has $766 and owns the mortgaged Pennsylvania Railroad. They have hotels on brown, light blue, and dark blue properties.

I mapped the Community Chest space 2 outcomes. Rolling a 2 lands on Income Tax for $200. A 3 lands on the mortgaged Reading Railroad. A 4 or 5 lands on light blue hotels worth $550 each. A 6 lands on Vermont at $550. A 7 lands on Connecticut at $600. An 8 lands on Jail. A 9 lands on St. Charles Place. A 10 lands on the mortgaged Electric Company.

Rolls 11 and 12 land on my own States and Virginia properties. The light blue hotels are all affordable with my current cash. Dark blue properties are too far away to reach this turn, and I will collect $200 from GO before passing them.

I can afford the $1500 Park Place hotel but would fall $139 short for Boardwalk. I am checking how much cash a pink hotel sale returns, since hotels cost the same as houses.

Selling a pink hotel returns $50 and replaces it with four houses. The bank has enough houses to do this. Standard pink rents drop from $750 to $625 once the hotel is sold.

Virginia Avenue's four-house rent is $700 and hotel rent is $900. I am weighing whether to sell a pink hotel now or wait until Boardwalk is reached. The turn has already rolled and passed GO, so this is strictly a post-turn decision.

I have decided against selling any pink hotels. Four-house rents would become payable by the opponent and I would lose the bankruptcy threat. Unmortgaging the Pennsylvania Railroad or Tennessee Avenue is negative expected value because it leaves no set and wastes cash for Boardwalk. Trading Tennessee Avenue would complete the opponent's orange monopoly. Trading cash would fund their dormant sets. I will keep both get-out-of-jail cards and end the turn.

I checked whether trading could help me acquire a new monopoly. The opponent already holds complete sets on oranges, reds, yellows, and greens, and they will not sell any of those properties. I am now considering whether to trade something useless for cash.

I ruled out trading the Pennsylvania Railroad. The opponent would need cash to unmortgage it, and I do not need that cash badly. I also noted that being in jail still allows rent collection, so using a get-out-of-jail card could be strategically useful later.

I will not trade. I have more cash than my opponent, so giving it away is unwise.

Unmortgaging would reduce my Boardwalk cushion. From position 2, reaching Park Place requires about five turns. The opponent sits on Pennsylvania Railroad at position 15, and St. Charles Place lies behind them.

The opponent is roughly 36 spaces away from the pink properties. They will pass GO and collect $200 before landing on them. The light blue hotels are reachable this next turn, with a roughly 39% chance of paying $550 to $600 in rent. The brown properties lie behind me and will be passed again on the next lap.

I am now treating this as a race. Paying $600 in light blue rent would leave me with $1261, which is still below the $1500 Park Place hotel and $2000 Boardwalk hotel. I will likely reach the dark blues before the opponent reaches the pinks, so I need to calculate bankruptcy lines carefully.

Virginia Avenue's $900 hotel rent is unaffordable from cash alone. The opponent could liquidate buildings to pay it. Selling a brown hotel returns half its cost, replacing it with four houses. Each house sells for $25. The bank holds 32 houses, so this conversion is possible.

Fully stripping a brown hotel returns $125 per property, or $250 total for both. Light blue hotels return $375 total when stripped. Dark blue hotels return $1000 total when stripped.

I rechecked the opponent's bankruptcy lines. With $766 cash, a $900 Virginia Avenue rent leaves a $134 shortfall. They could cover it by selling one brown or light blue hotel plus houses without touching dark blues. A $750 pink rent is barely payable with only $16 left over. That would bankrupt them or force a dark-blue downgrade.

A second $750 pink rent would still leave a $109 shortfall after liquidating light and brown properties. Virginia Avenue's $900 rent is also too large to cover from cash alone, so dark blue hotels would be damaged either way. I will keep the pink hotels as my win condition. Unmortgaging anything is still not worthwhile because it wastes cash for the dark blue cushion. From position 2, Boardwalk is 37 spaces away and GO is 38, so I cannot collect $200 before landing on Boardwalk.

I will land on Boardwalk before collecting the $200 GO bonus. After paying the $1500 Park Place rent, I would have only $361 left. That is far below the $2000 Boardwalk hotel. Selling one pink hotel for $50 would not cover the gap. I would need to liquidate most of my pink hotels to raise enough cash.

Selling all three pink hotels would raise only $750, bringing total cash to $1111. That is still $889 short of the $2000 Boardwalk hotel. Mortgaging is impossible because the pink properties have hotels that must be sold first. The opponent may also pay rent on my pinks before I reach Boardwalk.

I will not pre-sell any hotels. Doing so would remove the bankruptcy threat that could force the opponent to downgrade dark-blue hotels after pink hits. I might also collect rent from them before reaching the dark blues, and I cannot predict whether I will land on Park Place or Boardwalk.

Selling a pink hotel now would lower rent to $625 or $700, making it easier for the opponent to pay and reducing the bankruptcy threat. That is a poor tradeoff for only $50. I also considered trading something for cash, but the opponent would only want Tennessee Avenue to complete their orange monopoly, and giving that up would be catastrophic.

Unmortgaging two orange properties would cost about $209, leaving the opponent with roughly $557. That is enough to build several houses on the set and create dangerous hotel rent. I will never trade Tennessee Avenue. Get-out-of-jail-free cards are useless to them for building.

I will keep the get-out-of-jail-free cards for jail strategy. If I land in jail near the dark blues, staying there avoids paying rent on Park Place and Boardwalk while the opponent might hit my pink properties. I will not trade the Pennsylvania Railroad because the opponent already has three mortgaged railroads and would not pay much for it. I will end the turn with a short public message.

I rolled a 10 from position 32 to reach Community Chest at position 2. The $150 cash increase instead of $200 suggests the card was a $50 penalty such as a doctor's fee.
